questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which speech product follows accepted format expectations?

answer.text: A. A page of unrelated facts with no sections.

feedback.text: This does not show a clear format.

answer.text: B. An outline with introduction, focus, main points, support, transitions, and conclusion.

feedback.text: Correct. This follows a complete speech structure.

answer.text: C. A note that says "talk about school."

feedback.text: This is too vague and incomplete.

answer.text: D. A conclusion only.

feedback.text: A conclusion alone is not a complete speech product.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which note would best help a speaker present information orally?

answer.text: A. Say stuff about notes.

feedback.text: This is vague and not useful for organized speaking.

answer.text: B. Read every sentence from source.

feedback.text: This may lead to reading instead of presenting.

answer.text: C. Something about studying maybe.

feedback.text: This does not give a clear speech cue.

answer.text: D. Point 2: headings help students find sections quickly.

feedback.text: Correct. This note gives a clear point for delivery.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.04

Which sentence is conventionally correct?

answer.text: A. My presentation includes three organized main points.

feedback.text: Correct. The sentence uses standard capitalization and grammar.

answer.text: B. my presentation include three organized main points.

feedback.text: This has capitalization and agreement errors.

answer.text: C. My presentation include three organized point groups.

feedback.text: This has a subject-verb agreement error.

answer.text: D. my presentation includes three organized points.

feedback.text: This needs capitalization at the beginning before it follows standard English conventions.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

What does format help a speaker do?

answer.text: A. Hide the speech focus.

feedback.text: Format should make the focus clearer, not hide it.

answer.text: B. Avoid planning the speech.

feedback.text: Format is part of planning.

answer.text: C. Arrange speech parts so the message is clear.

feedback.text: Correct. Format supports clear communication.

answer.text: D. Replace every main point with a joke.

feedback.text: This weakens quality and organization.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which item is missing from this outline: introduction, focus, three points, support, transitions?

answer.text: A. Conclusion

feedback.text: Correct. A complete speech outline needs a conclusion to close the message.

answer.text: B. More unrelated facts

feedback.text: Unrelated facts do not complete the required format.

answer.text: C. Random title words

feedback.text: A title may help, but the missing major speech part is the conclusion.

answer.text: D. A longer font

feedback.text: Font length is not a speech format requirement.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which outline choice supports coherent oral presentation?

answer.text: A. Put main points in random order.

feedback.text: Random order makes the speech harder to follow.

answer.text: B. Add unrelated details between points.

feedback.text: Unrelated details weaken focus.

answer.text: C. Remove all transitions.

feedback.text: Transitions help listeners follow connections.

answer.text: D. Arrange main points in a logical sequence.

feedback.text: Correct. Logical order helps the audience follow the speech.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.04

Which revision fixes the sentence "my speech describe two types of transitions"?

answer.text: A. my speech describe transition types.

feedback.text: This keeps the original capitalization and agreement errors.

answer.text: B. My speech describe two types of transitions.

feedback.text: This fixes capitalization but not subject-verb agreement.

answer.text: C. My speech describes two types of transitions.

feedback.text: Correct. This fixes capitalization and agreement.

answer.text: D. my speech describes two transition types.

feedback.text: This still needs capitalization before it is ready for speech notes.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which checklist item best measures quality?

answer.text: A. The speech product has many words.

feedback.text: Many words do not guarantee clear communication.

answer.text: B. The conclusion introduces a new topic.

feedback.text: A conclusion should close the focus, not shift topics.

answer.text: C. The notes are hard to use while speaking.

feedback.text: Hard-to-use notes do not meet quality expectations.

answer.text: D. Each transition shows how ideas connect.

feedback.text: Correct. Useful transitions are a quality feature.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

What is the best reason to label parts of a speech outline?

answer.text: A. Labels make the structure easier to follow and check.

feedback.text: Correct. Labels help the speaker see whether the format is complete.

answer.text: B. Labels replace the need for support.

feedback.text: Support is still needed under main points.

answer.text: C. Labels make every idea correct automatically.

feedback.text: Labels help organization but do not guarantee content accuracy.

answer.text: D. Labels hide missing sections.

feedback.text: Labels should reveal missing sections, not hide them.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which note card is strongest for delivery?

answer.text: A. "Everything about planning."

feedback.text: This is too broad to guide delivery.

answer.text: B. "Read entire paragraph."

feedback.text: This may cause the speaker to read instead of present.

answer.text: C. "Point 1: planner lists deadlines; explain why visible deadlines help."

feedback.text: Correct. This gives a clear cue and a reasoning reminder.

answer.text: D. "Something next."

feedback.text: This is vague and not useful.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.04

Which sentence needs correction?

answer.text: A. My outline includes transitions between the main points.

feedback.text: This sentence uses standard English.

answer.text: B. my outline include transitions between the main points.

feedback.text: Correct. This needs capitalization and subject-verb agreement correction.

answer.text: C. The conclusion restates the focus of the speech.

feedback.text: This sentence is correct.

answer.text: D. Each point includes support and reasoning.

feedback.text: This sentence is correct.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which revision improves a weak speech product?

answer.text: A. Remove all headings from the outline.

feedback.text: Removing headings makes structure less clear.

answer.text: B. Delete the focus sentence.

feedback.text: The focus sentence is needed for organization.

answer.text: C. Add support under each main point.

feedback.text: Correct. Support helps the speech product meet quality expectations.

answer.text: D. Add unrelated stories to every section.

feedback.text: Unrelated stories weaken the format and focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which statement best describes quality expectations?

answer.text: A. Standards that help work become complete, clear, accurate, and ready for its purpose.

feedback.text: Correct. Quality expectations guide how well the product works.

answer.text: B. A rule that every speech must be as long as possible.

feedback.text: Length alone is not quality.

answer.text: C. A way to avoid checking grammar.

feedback.text: Conventions are part of quality.

answer.text: D. A reason to remove organization.

feedback.text: Organization supports quality.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Why should a speech outline include transitions?

answer.text: A. To make the speech less organized.

feedback.text: Transitions make the speech more organized.

answer.text: B. To add unrelated facts.

feedback.text: Transitions should connect related ideas.

answer.text: C. To replace the conclusion.

feedback.text: A conclusion is still needed.

answer.text: D. To guide listeners from one idea to the next.

feedback.text: Correct. Transitions support oral presentation by showing connections.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.04

Which correction is best for "the speaker use note cards"?

answer.text: A. the speaker use note cards

feedback.text: This keeps the original errors.

answer.text: B. The speaker use note cards.

feedback.text: This fixes capitalization but not agreement.

answer.text: C. The speaker uses note cards.

feedback.text: Correct. This uses capitalization and correct subject-verb agreement.

answer.text: D. the speaker uses note-card cues.

feedback.text: This fixes agreement but not capitalization.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which speech product is incomplete?

answer.text: A. Outline with focus, main points, support, transitions, and conclusion.

feedback.text: This includes major required parts.

answer.text: B. Note card with a clear point and evidence cue.

feedback.text: This can be a useful speech product.

answer.text: C. Checklist with format, support, transitions, and conventions.

feedback.text: This checks multiple quality expectations.

answer.text: D. Outline with only a title and no speech sections.

feedback.text: Correct. A title alone is incomplete.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which question should a speaker ask when checking format?

answer.text: A. Does my product include the required speech parts?

feedback.text: Correct. Format checking begins with required parts.

answer.text: B. Can I remove the focus?

feedback.text: Removing the focus weakens format and organization.

answer.text: C. Did I add unrelated material?

feedback.text: Unrelated material is a problem, not a format goal.

answer.text: D. Is my work confusing enough?

feedback.text: Quality expectations require clarity.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which conclusion best supports a quality speech format?

answer.text: A. I am done now, and I forgot my topic.

feedback.text: This does not close the speech focus.

answer.text: B. Planning ahead helps students manage deadlines, materials, and study time.

feedback.text: Correct. This restates the central idea and closes the speech.

answer.text: C. Here is a new topic I did not mention earlier.

feedback.text: A conclusion should not introduce an unrelated topic.

answer.text: D. My speech had some words in it.

feedback.text: This is vague and does not summarize the focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.04

Which sentence is ready for submission?

answer.text: A. my note cards helps presentation delivery.

feedback.text: This has capitalization and agreement errors.

answer.text: B. My note cards helps me present.

feedback.text: This has a subject-verb agreement error.

answer.text: C. My note cards help me present.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence follows standard English conventions.

answer.text: D. my note cards support my presentation.

feedback.text: This needs capitalization before it follows standard English conventions.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

What is the best revision for a note card that says "say all the things"?

answer.text: A. Keep it because it is short.

feedback.text: Short notes must still be useful.

answer.text: B. Add more vague words.

feedback.text: Vague wording does not improve quality.

answer.text: C. Delete every cue from the card.

feedback.text: The speaker still needs useful cues.

answer.text: D. Replace it with a specific point and support cue.

feedback.text: Correct. A note card should guide the speaker clearly.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which item belongs on a speech quality checklist?

answer.text: A. Main points are in logical order.

feedback.text: Correct. Logical order is part of quality speech organization.

answer.text: B. Every sentence is copied from a source.

feedback.text: Copying is not a quality expectation for speech notes.

answer.text: C. The outline avoids a conclusion.

feedback.text: A conclusion is usually required.

answer.text: D. The speaker uses no support.

feedback.text: Support is needed for quality development.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which choice best supports coherent focus in a speech product?

answer.text: A. Each main point supports the same focus.

feedback.text: Correct. Coherent focus means the parts work together.

answer.text: B. Each main point changes to a new topic.

feedback.text: Changing topics weakens coherence.

answer.text: C. The conclusion ignores the focus.

feedback.text: A conclusion should return to the focus.

answer.text: D. The outline includes unrelated facts.

feedback.text: Unrelated facts break focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.04

What should a speaker check before submitting speech notes?

answer.text: A. Whether errors make the notes harder to understand.

feedback.text: This is a useful concern, but the best answer names the convention check directly.

answer.text: B. Whether capitalization, spelling, punctuation, and grammar are correct.

feedback.text: Correct. These are standard English conventions.

answer.text: C. Whether all words are lowercase.

feedback.text: All-lowercase writing is not standard English.

answer.text: D. Whether the notes avoid punctuation.

feedback.text: Punctuation supports clarity.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which format problem should be fixed first?

answer.text: A. The outline has one extra clear support detail.

feedback.text: An extra relevant detail may not be the biggest format problem.

answer.text: B. The outline has no main points.

feedback.text: Correct. Main points are essential speech format parts.

answer.text: C. The introduction has a clear focus statement.

feedback.text: This is a strength, not a problem.

answer.text: D. The note card uses a precise academic word.

feedback.text: Precise academic words can improve quality.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_Quiz_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which statement best summarizes this lesson?

answer.text: A. Quality speech products should avoid transitions.

feedback.text: Transitions support organization and quality.

answer.text: B. Quality speech products only need to be long.

feedback.text: Length alone does not show quality.

answer.text: C. Quality speech products do not need checking.

feedback.text: Checking is part of producing polished work.

answer.text: D. Quality speech products follow the required format, organize ideas clearly, and use standard English conventions.

feedback.text: Correct. This summarizes format-specific quality work.
